description: Shared case table for the merchant identity normaliser. The Python `normalize_key` (app/services/email_sync_services/merchant_rules.py) and the frontend TS port (features/merchants/data/matching.ts) MUST both reproduce this table exactly; it is the only thing keeping the two from drifting.
algorithm: 2. replace every run of characters outside [a-z0-9] with a single ASCII space (applied AFTER lowercasing, so non-ASCII letters are dropped, and digits are KEPT on purpose: 'carrefour 402' and 'carrefour 118' are different merchants)
4. truncate to the first 120 characters (no re-trim afterwards, so a truncated key may end in a space)

5. FIXED POINT: because step 4 truncates AFTER trimming, a key longer than 120 characters can end in a space (see the last case). The server re-normalises whatever the client sends, which trims that space, so a client must apply the function twice (or trim the result) before it stores or compares the key — otherwise its local key and the server's stored key differ by one trailing space.

cases.input: SUPERMARKET SUPERMARKET SUPERMARKET SUPERMARKET SUPERMARKET SUPERMARKET SUPERMARKET SUPERMARKET SUPERMARKET SUPERMARKET SUPERMARKET SUPERMARKET
cases.expected: supermarket supermarket supermarket supermarket supermarket supermarket supermarket supermarket supermarket supermarket
